mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which in turn predicts negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the rank information coefficient (IC) over the next 5 years is not statistically significant (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of simultaneous supply shocks.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending power and corporate profit margins, predicting negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the mechanism does not activate during a confirmed recession.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces input demand and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered months, or the effect reverses during periods of strong demand growth.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a monetary policy tightening coinciding with rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when GDP growth is accelerating.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above their 6-month moving averages signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of high inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate below 4.5% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average signals a robust residential construction cycle, which boosts demand for materials and capital goods and predicts positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the effect is not present during periods of rising mortgage rates.
